text: Truth does not oppose truth; rather, it accords with it and bears witness to it.
author: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
meaning: Averroes — the Andalusian Muslim philosopher who served the Almohad court in Marrakech — argued that reason and revelation are two roads to the same truth: when they seem to clash, the fault lies in our interpretation, not in truth itself. It remains one of history's most influential arguments that philosophy, science, and faith can ultimately agree.

text: The unexamined life is not worth living.
author: Socrates
meaning: A life lived on autopilot — never questioning your beliefs, choices, or values — misses what being human is for. It is the founding call of Western philosophy to examine how you think, not just what you think.

text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca
meaning: Most of our fears never arrive; the mind rehearses disasters that never happen. Learning to notice that gap between imagined and actual pain is the beginning of Stoic calm.

text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
author: Seneca
meaning: Poverty is measured by desire, not by possessions. Whoever endlessly wants more stays poor no matter how much they own; whoever wants little is already rich.

text: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
author: Marcus Aurelius
meaning: Obstacles are not detours from the plan — handled rightly, they are the raw material the plan is made of. Each block in the road is a chance to practice exactly the virtue the road was testing.

text: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
author: Epictetus
meaning: Events are neutral; it is our judgment about them that wounds or delights us. Between what happens and how you feel sits your own interpretation — and that, unlike the event, is yours to change.

text: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
meaning: The closing line of the Tractatus: some things cannot be said in precise language, only shown or lived. Knowing the limit of language, Wittgenstein thought, is part of knowing the world honestly.

text: The owl of Minerva spreads its wings only with the falling of the dusk.
author: G.W.F. Hegel
meaning: Understanding arrives only after events have unfolded, like the owl of wisdom flying at nightfall. Philosophy explains life backward, not forward — so be humble about predicting where history is going.

text: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
source: Twilight of the Idols, Maxims and Arrows
meaning: Purpose, not comfort, is what carries people through hardship. Find your reason — and the conditions you must endure become survivable, even meaningful.

text: Man is condemned to be free.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre
meaning: Thrown into the world without a script, you must choose — and every choice defines who you are. Even refusing to choose is a choice you own; there is no hiding from responsibility for your life.

text: Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.
author: Simone Weil
meaning: Truly attending to a person or a problem — full, patient, undistracted presence — is one of the rarest gifts you can give, rarer than money or advice. Attention, for Weil, is also the heart of prayer and of real study.

text: When you see a worthy person, think of equaling them; when you see an unworthy one, examine yourself.
author: Confucius
meaning: Other people are mirrors: admiration should turn into emulation, and annoyance should turn inward into self-examination. Every encounter becomes material for improving your own character.

text: The wound is the place where the Light enters you.
author: Rumi
meaning: Brokenness is not the end of the story but the opening through which growth, compassion, and wisdom enter. Suffering honestly faced becomes the very place transformation happens.
